steps.what: Choose treatment and prescribe medication for the sick or injured animal where appropriate
Treat the animal through indicated bone setting, wound care or surgery

tasks.design: Keep treatment decisions and prescriptions with the veterinarian in the veterinary clinical system {OTHER}. Hands-on treatment remains with the authorised clinical team; no model selects a drug, dose or surgical action.
tasks.previous_blocker: Treatment depends on the animal's condition, species, response and clinical judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing veterinary records support decisions without replacing treatment.
tasks.still_hard: Complications, uncertain diagnosis and species-specific risks.
tasks.human_edge: Adapting treatment to the animal and responding to complications.
tasks.altitude: Clinical authority and treatment time remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Delegation limits and escalation of adverse responses

evidence.claim: Human-care medication surveillance in the digest does not establish veterinary prescribing or treatment automation; no treatment saving is proposed.

assumptions: Boundary is treatment choice, prescribing where indicated and physical treatment. Bone setting, wound care and surgery are alternative clinical routes, not compulsory stages for every animal. Diagnosis, owner counselling and separate records are outside this task.
No machine depends on a free diagnosis, weight or contraindication code. Clinical assessment and treatment retain full time; no new capture process is introduced.
Native veterinary records come first. National veterinary rules apply; human-care prescribing rules in the digest are not transferred to animals.
Zero incremental upkeep because no new treatment system is introduced. Support-team work and owner decision time are outside the veterinarian denominator and unchanged.
unknowns: National veterinary prescribing rules and delegation arrangements
research_questions: Which treatment-support tasks are separate measurable activities rather than part of direct clinical work?

approvals.approved_version: Exact animal identity, selected treatment and any prescription drug, dose, route and duration; changes void veterinary approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gives net0 after zero upkeep. Treatment decisions30 and physical treatment70 retain full time; existing system runtime earns no saving.

steps.what: Operate radiographic or ultrasound equipment to acquire diagnostically useful animal images
Interpret resulting images against the animal's history and examination findings

tasks.design: Use existing acquisition controls and image access in the veterinary imaging system {OTHER}. Retain positioning, image adequacy and clinical interpretation with the veterinarian; human mammography results in the digest do not validate animal image interpretation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Useful images require appropriate acquisition and interpretation in species-specific context.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing imaging equipment supports acquisition without demonstrating a new labour saving.
tasks.still_hard: Movement, unusual anatomy, artefacts and findings needing specialist review.
tasks.human_edge: Combining imaging with examination and recognising diagnostic uncertainty.
tasks.altitude: Acquisition and interpretation responsibilities stay unchanged.

reach.learn: Referral quality and limits of image interpretation

evidence.claim: The digest's human imaging products and mammography trial do not establish validated veterinary radiography or ultrasound automation.

assumptions: Boundary is acquisition and interpretation, not later treatment or a separate written report. Radiography and ultrasound are alternative modalities. Support-personnel and specialist work are excluded and unchanged.
No new machine consumes an assumed animal anatomy or normality label; image capture and interpretation remain in s1/s2 with full time retained.
Native image functions come first. Zero upkeep because no new imaging model or integration is proposed; national veterinary equipment and radiation rules must be confirmed locally.
unknowns: Available equipment and specialist review arrangements
research_questions: Which imaging findings require specialist interpretation rather than an additional automated measurement?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gives net0 after zero upkeep. Acquisition60 and interpretation40 remain fully counted; no human-imaging benchmark is transferred.

tasks.short: Educate the public about zoonotic disease

steps.what: Select current zoonotic disease guidance appropriate to the audience and local concerns
Prepare plain-language educational explanations about diseases spread from animals to humans

loop.purpose: Adapt checked zoonotic guidance into a plain-language education draft
loop.input: Veterinarian-selected source excerpts, audience and approved scope
loop.output: Draft explanation with source references and no personal diagnosis
loop.check: Veterinarian checks transmission, prevention, uncertainty and escalation advice against the exact sources; no invented outbreak or risk estimate
loop.stop: Outdated source, conflicting guidance or unsupported advice requires manual material preparation
loop.why_not_simpler: Reuse existing approved leaflets first; a varied audience may still require bounded rewriting

steps.what: Check and deliver the education, answering questions and correcting misunderstandings

tasks.design: Reuse approved public guidance from {DOCS} first. Where new wording is required, a bounded draft adapts only selected source excerpts, and the veterinarian checks every prevention claim before delivery while keeping public questions and discussion fully human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Relevant public guidance can need adaptation for the audience.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded source-based rewriting is feasible, but the digest establishes no veterinary education outcome or measured saving.
tasks.still_hard: Changing guidance, alarmist interpretations and questions needing medical rather than veterinary advice.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining proportionate prevention and recognising when to refer questions to public-health professionals.
tasks.altitude: Potentially less preparation wording; source selection and public discussion stay unchanged.

reach.learn: Audience comprehension and current public-health escalation routes

evidence.claim: Source-based educational rewriting is model knowledge; the digest's human patient-information source does not establish veterinary zoonosis education capability or savings.

assumptions: Boundary is preparing and delivering public education, not diagnosing exposures or outbreak surveillance. The scenario applies only when the veterinarian currently prepares fresh wording; direct reuse of existing leaflets earns no new saving.

Veterinarian s1 produces source title/version/date, relevant excerpts, audience, scope and approved prevention messages within its full20 hours. No machine depends on a free outbreak flag or structured disease-risk score. Missing or disputed sources cause manual preparation.

Native approved-content reuse comes first. s2 retains15 hours for corrections; s3 retains55 for final content checking, delivery and questions. Changed material invalidates approval before presentation.
Incremental4 focal hours cover source currency and output sampling, including any new adaptation checks. No unpaid content-maintenance role is assumed.
unknowns: Existing education materials and actual new-wording effort
Audience needs and authoritative veterinary/public-health sources
research_questions: Can preparation wording fall while prevention accuracy and audience understanding remain at least as good?

already_counted.description: Draft correction and final education checks and delivery

approvals.approved_version: Exact education wording, source versions, prevention messages and intended audience; changes void veterinarian approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R90 gives gross10 and net6 after4 upkeep. High assumes preparation25 falls to15; low is manual preparation plus4 upkeep. Source selection20 and final checking/delivery55 remain unchanged. E1 scenario.

tasks.short: Counsel owners about pet death or euthanasia

steps.what: Counsel clients about pet deaths or euthanasia decisions with compassion and clinical context

tasks.design: Keep grief support and euthanasia discussion with the veterinarian. Existing care information in {DOCS} may help explain options, but it does not replace a compassionate conversation or decide for the owner.
tasks.previous_blocker: Owners need individual support in a difficult and emotionally consequential situation.
tasks.enabler_now: Information access helps explain choices without replacing empathy and trust.
tasks.still_hard: Uncertainty about suffering, conflicting family views and guilt after a loss.
tasks.human_edge: Listening without pressure and explaining clinical limits sensitively.
tasks.altitude: Counselling responsibility and time stay unchanged.

reach.learn: Appropriate referral and emotional support boundaries

evidence.claim: Documentation or patient-information tools do not establish replacement of grief counselling or euthanasia discussions.

assumptions: Boundary is owner counselling, not performing euthanasia, recording consent or clinical treatment. Those remain distinct tasks. Owner time is excluded and unchanged.
No machine consumes a free quality-of-life or euthanasia recommendation score. All interpretation and conversation remain in s1.
Native information access comes first. Zero upkeep because no new counselling service, model or materials are introduced.
unknowns: Available owner support and referral arrangements
research_questions: What further support do owners need after the clinical discussion?

already_counted.description: Compassionate discussion and responses to owner concerns

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gives net0 after zero upkeep. Owner counselling retains full time; no record-writing or treatment saving is added.

reach: Coordinate specialist imaging, veterinary nursing and public-health messages
